chunks: The congregational prayer on Friday is an obligatory duty (farida wajiba), and on other days it is sunnah. Whoever abandons it out of disdain for it and for the congregation of the Muslims, without any excuse, then there is no prayer counted for him.

The Friday prayer has been lifted from nine: the minor (child), the elderly, the insane, the traveler, the slave, the woman, the sick, the blind, and one who is at a distance of two parasangs (approx. 12 km).
The prayer of a man in congregation surpasses the prayer of a man alone by twenty-five degrees in Paradise.

key_terms.درجة في الجنة: Degrees/ranks in Paradise — the spiritual reward is described in terms of elevated stations in the afterlife
key_terms.فريضة واجبة: An obligatory duty — a doubling of emphasis (farida = obligatory act, wajiba = mandatory) to stress the binding nature of Friday congregational prayer
key_terms.فَرْسَخَيْن: Two parasangs — a unit of distance (approx. 5-6 km each), so about 12 km total; this is the minimum distance that exempts a person from Friday prayer
key_terms.وُضِعَتْ: Has been lifted/exempted — a jurisprudential term indicating that the obligation is removed from these nine categories

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from Friday Jumu'ah prayer in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the legal ruling on Friday (Jumu'ah) congregational prayer: it is obligatory on Fridays and recommended on other days. It lists nine categories of people exempt from this obligation — minors, the elderly, the insane, travelers, slaves, women, the sick, the blind, and those beyond two parasangs. The hadith also emphasizes the immense spiritual reward of congregational prayer, which surpasses individual prayer by twenty-five ranks in Paradise.

en.bilal-muhammad: The jama`a on the day of Jum`a is a wajib farida, and in the rest of the days [it is] a sunna. One who abandons it out of disdain of it and of the jama`a of the Muslims without a reason (or, illness), then there is no prayer counted for him.
Jum`a has been unburdened from nine: from the minor, the senior, the insane, the traveler, the slave, the woman, the sick, the blind, and one who is on the head (i.e. distance) of two parasangs.
The prayer of the man in jama`a is superior to the prayer of the man alone by himself by twenty-five degrees in Paradise.
